answersReviewFindings.finding: Finding A (role_keep.go:507): a failed first resolution of the holder ends the handover at Debug and reports nothing, so the copies wait for the 5-minute sweep, whose handover can end the same way, and they age past roleKeepWindow with nothing above Debug. The doc's premise was false: resolveRoleHolder errs only when a read failed, and a role nobody holds comes back roleHolderUnclaimed with a nil error, which the handover already ends on.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The reviewer's one rule, applied to both reads. walked and holderUnresolved are gone; one retry(line, cause) closure writes the read's Debug line and then reads cfg.registry.CachedRoleHolder(role). A claim naming a session earns the next pause and sets readErr, so ended() carries the failure out and reportKeptRoleDrain logs it at Error; a role no claim names, or a claim read that itself failed, ends the handover at Debug. Both false premises are deleted from the docs.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestAHandoverOfAClaimedRoleRetriesAHolderResolutionThatFailed, which fails at a4b9ededf432 with 'the handover forwarded [], want [envoy.role.forward.kept-holder-read-00]: a resolution that did not answer is retried, not read as a role nobody holds'.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Finding B (role_keep.go:529): the lane-read retry has no exit for a role nobody holds, so an undecodable cursor or a refusing bus costs the full 10-minute handover window and about 25 reads; and hold was a plain Lock that did not see ctx while runKeptRoleDrain started its window before it, so every keep for that role queued one more goroutine on the guard, each logging its own Error line.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The same rule ends an unclaimed role's handover at once at Debug, so the retry runs only while the role is claimed. roleKeepGuards' per-role guard is now a channel of one: hold(ctx, role) (func(), bool) gives the wait up when ctx ends, so a handover whose window has run out queues nothing behind one that is failing through its window; tryHold keeps its meaning for the sweep; drainKeptRole reports nothing when the guard was not taken.
answersReviewFindings.test: TestAHandoverForAnUnclaimedRoleEndsOnACursorNoReadCanDecode (fails at a4b9ededf432, reporting the undecodable cursor after 3.29 s of retries; 0.04 s and nothing reported here) and TestAKeptLaneGuardStopsWaitingWhenTheHandoversContextEnds, the architect's third test for the round, which shows a second hold waiting, returning false within 10 s of its context ending, and leaving the guard with its first holder.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor role_keep.go:493: holderUnresolved has one caller, the backoff pair appears three times, and ended() is returned at two exits while err is returned at five, which agree only because headErr is reset every pass with nothing saying so.
answersReviewFindings.fix: One retry() closure for both reads, one waitOut() for the three backoff pairs, ended() returned at every exit, and readErr reset once per pass right after the pause with that invariant stated in the code and in the function's doc. roleKeepDrainBackoff's doc now covers a failed head read.
answersReviewFindings.test: No new test: the handover tests of rounds 3 to 6 drive every branch of the rewritten loop and pass unchanged, which is what 'the behaviour does not change' means here.

answersReviewFindings.finding: Minor role_keep.go:665: since the sweep no longer reads the head it starts a handover for every claimed role with any kept copy, drained lanes included, and logged 'found a lane no handover was draining' for each.
answersReviewFindings.fix: The line is now 'listener kept role sweep is handing over a claimed role's kept lane', true of a drained lane as of any other, and the sweep's doc no longer claims a passed-over unclaimed lane is logged, since nothing is logged for it. The line stays at the sweep rather than moving into the handover: the sweep's decision is what it records, and the handover's own end is already reported by reportKeptRoleDrain.
answersReviewFindings.test: None; prose and a log line.
